Figure 1. Multimodal memory and predictive test-time adaptation in M2AdaptVLA. (a) Visual memory cues the next key, while wrench
memory signals a completed press. With direct injection, the action expert implicitly learns how much to rely on wrench memory. The
context gate weights wrench history by task stage. (b) The TTT bank provides an implicit progress cue and retains history beyond the frame
window, outperforming the frame bank on progress tracking, initial-scene recall, and demonstration following. (c) Raising the board changes
contact dynamics. Schematic traces show how wrench forecast errors guide online adaptation to this shift.
